items.question: Which gas do we need to breathe in to stay alive?
items.explanation: Our body uses oxygen to get energy from food. We breathe in oxygen and breathe out carbon dioxide. Green plants do the opposite during the day.

items.question: Most of the air around us is nitrogen.
items.explanation: Air is about 78% nitrogen and about 21% oxygen. The rest is small amounts of argon, carbon dioxide and other gases. So oxygen is important, but nitrogen is the biggest part.

items.question: Which light gas is used to fill party balloons so they float, and does not catch fire?
items.explanation: Helium is lighter than air, so balloons filled with it float up. Hydrogen is also light but catches fire very easily, so helium is much safer.

items.fact: Noble gases like neon and argon hardly ever react with other substances. They are also called inert gases.
items.explanation: Their atoms are already stable, so they do not need to react. Neon glows bright red-orange in signboards. Argon is filled inside some bulbs to protect the thin wire.

items.question: Which gas turns clear lime water milky?
items.explanation: Carbon dioxide reacts with lime water (calcium hydroxide) to form calcium carbonate. Calcium carbonate does not dissolve, so the water looks milky. You can see this by blowing through a straw into lime water.
